newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices steady to up with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices steady to up with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to higher again Monday in sluggish trade, still underpinned by firm crude and tight East Coast high sulphur avails, industry sources said.

"I was waiting for a dip, but we're getting too close to winter for it to dip now. There's not much supply, and everyone's looking at crude," said one East Coast trader, adding dwindling East Coast bunkers have helped tighten HSFO.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs were talked firmer, with 2.2 percent up 35 cents to about $20.50 a barrel and three percent gaining slightly to near the $20 mark, traders said.
Physical one percent in New York was unchanged at $21.25, with November paper little changed at $21.50-65 and December also steady at $21.55-70, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices notionally were stable, with one percent still just over $20 and three percent at $20.25.

While some said a 200,000-barrel USG three percent deal reportedly done Friday at $19.25 was below-market, they said high sulphur supplies in the region seemed to be improving and may portend softer prices soon.
No NYH or USG deals were reported done today.

New York City gate gas prices firmed about five cents Monday to the low-$2.80s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid still at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent. November-March winter quotes for New York gas were at NYMEX plus $1.05-1.15, or in the $3.60-3.75 area.
